title: Go where learning is (Avot 4:14)
hookLine: every lecture is online, so why go anywhere? Nehorai: exile yourself to a place of Torah
tomorrow: the wrong show won. is there an answer for why?

cards: Every lecture is recorded now. Every tutorial is a search away. So can you learn it just as well from home?
The Talmud answers with a story. There was a sage named Rabbi Elazar ben Arach, and his own teacher, in Avot, called him an ever-flowing spring.

One day he went to a town known for its wine and its waters, and he liked it, and he stayed. When he finally came back, he was called up to read from the Torah in front of everyone. He opened the scroll.
And the words came out wrong.

teach.b: The verse was about the new month. He read it as something about a deaf heart, swapping letters that look alike. His learning, the Talmud says, had been forgotten.
The sages prayed for him, and it came back. And right there the Talmud brings a saying from Pirkei Avot.

teach.h: EXILE YOURSELF TO A PLACE OF TORAH.
teach.b: Rabbi Nehorai says: exile yourself to a place of Torah. Don't say it will come after you.
Your companions will make it firm in your hand. And don't lean on your own understanding. The Talmud even records a view that Nehorai was Elazar ben Arach himself, under another name.
Here's the turn. The ever-flowing spring didn't lose his learning by being lazy. He lost it by being somewhere it wasn't, without the people who kept it alive.
Learning, in this saying, isn't a file you carry. It's held in a place, by companions, the ones who argue with you and catch your mistakes. That's why Nehorai says go.
Don't wait for it to come after you. Not every move has to be a big one: a study partner, a class, a table where people read together.

how: Many Jews learn in a beit midrash, a study hall, or with a chavruta, a study partner, and some leave home for a season or a year to study in a yeshiva or seminary.

games.q: what does “go where learning is” mean?
o: travel the world to collect wisdom from every land
move toward the place and people where Torah is studied
stay where you are and wait for teachers to arrive

games.q: the story and the saying — tap the pairs.
p: a town of wine and waters
prayed, and his learning came back
exile yourself to a place of Torah

s: if you learned something well once, it stays with you anywhere
the ever-flowing spring forgot his learning when he stayed where it wasn't.
Nehorai says your companions will make the learning firm in your hand
learning is held by a place and by the people who learn with you.
the Talmud records a view that Nehorai was Elazar ben Arach
it brings that view right after telling his story.

games.q: you've been teaching yourself guitar from videos for a year and you've stalled. a local group meets weekly to play together, twenty minutes away. what does Nehorai's saying point to?
o: go to the group; companions make learning firm in a way videos can't.
stay home; you can find any lesson online, so it'll come to you.
quit for now; if it were meant to stick, it would have stuck.
games.why: don't say it will come after you. learning lives where people practice it together, and they're the ones who catch your mistakes.

practice: Stand up and walk, slowly, for about a minute, to the spot where you learn best: a desk, a chair by a window, a kitchen table.
When you get there, sit down, and for the rest of the sit, think of the one person you'd most like learning across from you.

wordCard.voice: Go where learning is. Rabbi Nehorai: exile yourself to a place of Torah, and let your companions make it firm.

orig.note: Hebrew: exile yourself to a place of Torah, Rabbi Nehorai's opening words.

carryVoice: For the road: go where learning is, because it won't come after you. Thirty-seven of sixty, until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Mishnah Avot 4:14 (Rabbi Nehorai: exile yourself to a place of Torah)
Babylonian Talmud, Shabbat 147b (Rabbi Elazar ben Arach forgets his learning; the misread verse; Nehorai identified with him by one view)
Mishnah Avot 2:8 (Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai calls Elazar ben Arach an ever-flowing spring)
